question.problem: The displacement $s,$ in meters, relative to a fixed origin $O$ of a particle moving in a straight line along the $x$-axis is given by $s(t)=(3t+1){e}^{-t}$, where $t\ge 0$ is the time measured in seconds. Determine the time intervals in which the particle is moving in the direction of decreasing $x.$
question.worked_solution:
If the particle moves in the direction of decreasing $x,$ then its velocity is negative. 

First, we calculate the velocity function by differentiating the position function:

$$
\begin{aligned}v(t) & =\frac{\text{d}s}{\text{d}t} \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}((3t+1){e}^{-t}) \\  & =(2-3t){e}^{-t}\end{aligned}
$$

To calculate time intervals in which the particle is moving in the direction of decreasing $x$, we solve the inequality $v(t)<0:$

$$
\begin{aligned}v(t) & <0 \\ (2-3t){e}^{-t} & <0 \\ 2-3t & <0 \\ 3t & >2 \\ t & >\frac{2}{3}\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, the time interval in which the particle is moving to the direction of decreasing $x$ is $t\in (\frac{2}{3},\infty ).$
